disputes.reason: Defensible as true: Basel large-exposure rules recognise eligible collateral/CRM, and valuing it at market is standard; the explanation that collateral must never be considered is too absolute.
Soft 'may have' claim is literally true (loans can outlast collateral, e.g. partly unsecured); ambiguous whether it states fact or best practice.

Defines unexpected loss as a tail-percentile loss, contradicting the standard definition (standard deviation of losses, EC = CM x UL) used by other cards in the deck; candidates could argue either way.
Explanation teaches UL as a tail-percentile measure, inconsistent with UL as the standard deviation of credit losses taught elsewhere; label is safe but the explanation is contested.
Truth depends on the UL definition: if UL is a tail-percentile loss (as another card states) it does rise with confidence level, so the card contradicts the deck.
Not clearly wrong: staff age/experience review may reasonably include diversity data; false only because it was not on the reading's list, not because the claim is incorrect.
